root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Grünfeld Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bf5 6. Ne5 c6 7. g4

overview: In the Scandinavian Classical line White plays 6.Ne5 c6 7.g4, kicking the Bf5. Black usually retreats ...Bg6 and White plays Nxg6 hxg6 with a kingside pawn advance, or ...Bg6 and the knight stays on e5. White gets space and attacking chances; Black must be careful about the pawn storm and the Black queen on a5.

white_ideas.idea: Push g4 and gain kingside space
Develop Bg2, Bd2 and castle long

black_ideas.idea: Retreat the bishop and hit the centre with ...e6 and ...c5
Counter with the queen on a5 and ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: White kingside pawns advanced to g4
Semi-open d-file with Black queen on a5

character.notes: A sharp line where White attacks the bishop and pushes pawns.

soundness.notes: A principled and sound line for both.

approach.notes: A recognised branch of the Scandinavian.

level.notes: Sharp pawn storms and forced bishop retreats need prep.

character.reason: White pawn storm and opposite plans make it double-edged.

level.reason: Some theory but not as deep as Advanced lines.

plans.reason: White advances the g-pawn at the bishop.
